title: Board games and their accessories
summary: Tabletop games in TCG Card Shop Simulator are stocked as sets with parts of their own: the game keeps a play mat, a deck box and a comic book as separate pieces of one set.
body: A tabletop game is stocked as a set. The game keeps one as a set with its own record, which is why it is ordered and displayed differently from a pack of cards.
A set has named parts. A play mat, a deck box and a comic book are each a kind of their own inside the set, so what arrives is made of identified pieces rather than one anonymous box.
Those parts are modelled. Each one has its own mesh in the game, which is why a set can be laid out with its mat and its boxes rather than only shown as a picture.
The games have names. The game ships icons for particular tabletop games, so the range is a defined list rather than a single generic board game.
Restocking them has its own screen. Tabletop games are restocked through a screen of their own rather than the ordinary item list, which is why they sit apart from the card stock.
They are a different trade from cards. Because the set is its own kind of stock, a tabletop game is another product line rather than more of the same inventory.
What this entry does not tell you: what any set costs, how many games exist, or whether customers prefer them to cards. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: A tabletop game is kept as a set with its own record.
A set has named parts: a play mat, a deck box and a comic book.
The build ships tabletop games as named meshes, including one called Mafia Works and one called Necromansters, with a dice box and its own material.
Each of those parts has its own mesh in the game.
Tabletop games restock through a screen of their own.
The game ships icons for particular tabletop games.
The build names further tabletop pieces, including a claim marker and a system gate, along with a card table of its own.
A second system gate and a set called Necro are named beside them.
The box art the game ships for these games names a claim game and two System Gate battle boxes.
The tabletop line has stock items of its own, named for the board-game range rather than for a single game.
The system-gate set is backed by its own material and sheet beside the mesh.
The game even carries an emote for throwing dice at the table.
